name: Sarah H. Wu
title: PhD student in Media Psychology
bio: Through my research, I aim to identify and address situations where technology has the potential to undermine human capacities. For example: How can we provide helpful content recommendations for today's parents, whose children are growing up in an algorithmically curated media environment? What drives people to rely on chatbots for interpersonal advice, and what are the consequences of doing so?

Before starting my PhD, I earned my BA in Psychology from Reed College in Portland, OR, and I was a predoctoral research fellow at the Stanford Institute for Research in the Social Sciences (IRiSS) and the Stanford Social Media Lab.

Outside of research, I play violin semi-professionally in Argentine tango ensembles across the Bay Area, including Orquesta Tipica Tarareando. I'm also an "adopted musician" of the Peninsula Symphony, and I volunteer for their  outreach program by playing assembly concerts for schools in underserved communities.
